newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels free 20 hostages, 83 left.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels free 20 hostages, 83 left.

text.p: The Marxist rebels holding hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima released 20 more hostages on Saturday, leaving a total of 83 inside the compound, live television showed.

Clad in crumpled suits, the freed hostages left the fortified compound during their 11th day in captivity, walking in single-file and smiling to waiting journalists. They boarded a bus outside the residence.

The rebels released the Dominican Republic ambassador, Jose Diaz, the president of the Peruvian Association of Exporters, Enrique Pendavis and the Malaysian ambassador, Ahmad Mokhtar, in an initial group, said Michel Minnig of the Red Cross, the official mediator in the crisis.

Following the reading of a statement by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, in which they said they "deplored" being labeled as terrorists, the guerrillas freed the 20 hostages, who were driven off to a local police hospital.
The freed hostages included Peruvian diplomats and Japanese business executives, according to the Red Cross, who read out a list of the names of the released captives.

The release followed the first face-to-face contact between the rebels and a government negotiator after Peru's chief mediator, Education Minister Domingo Palermo, spent three hours and 15 minutes inside the compound earlier Saturday.
